objects.name: Analytic 2268
objects.description: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) Windows service (Open Platform Communications (OPC) server, historian, Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) polling service) consuming abnormal Central Processing Unit (CPU)/memory resources and becoming unresponsive following receipt of a high volume of connections to its application port, correlated with watchdog timeout or service crash events. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when a device-specific traffic/resource threshold is exceeded and the same window shows service degradation, failed polling, device alarm/restart, resource exhaustion, or malformed/out-of-spec protocol behavior. Suppress planned load tests, maintenance, network convergence/failover, and known equipment faults after operator confirmation.

x_mitre_log_source_references.channel: Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational Event ID 3 NetworkConnect: inbound connection rate to Industrial Control Systems (ICS) application port exceeds threshold per minute from unexpected sources

x_mitre_log_source_references.name: WinEventLog:System
x_mitre_log_source_references.channel: EventCode=7034, 7036 for Industrial Control Systems (ICS) service within detection window of connection flood

x_mitre_mutable_elements.description: Network device CPU utilization percentage above which sustained load suggests packet-processing strain from flood traffic.
Connections-per-minute threshold exceeding normal SCADA polling cadence, derived from the device's actual configured scan rate.
Time window over which flood rate and subsequent device silence are correlated, typically 1-5 minutes.
Device-specific supervisory poll interval used to determine what counts as a process historian gap.
Deviation from baseline interface error/discard rate, tuned against historical interface health data.
Number of malformed/out-of-spec PDUs within the detection window constituting a flood, set above the device's documented error-tolerance baseline.
